//: Copy to ~/.claude-dashboard/watchers.json and fill in real IDs. This file is a template with placeholders only. Bot tokens are read from a reference (env var / Keychain / file), never stored here.
//version: Schema version. A pre-v2 file (top-level slack.botToken, trigger.type 'mention', watcher.channels, intents[]) is migrated in memory at load time and keeps working as-is — nothing rewrites it.
//slack.bots: One entry per Slack bot, keyed by a ref a watcher points at via trigger.botRef ('default' when omitted). 'token' is a REFERENCE: '$ENV_VAR', 'keychain:<service>[:<account>]' (macOS Keychain, preferred), or '@/abs/path' to a chmod-600 file. A bare string is shorthand for { token }. 'label' is only for display.
//rate-limits: Every Slack call is queued through one shared, self-throttling pacer (serial, min gap, backs off on 429). Tune with CLAUDE_DASH_SLACK_MIN_GAP_MS (default 1200) and CLAUDE_DASH_SLACK_MAX_GAP_MS. Cost per pass = channels + tracked threads; CLAUDE_DASH_WATCHER_THREAD_TTL_DAYS shortens the thread set.

watchers.//: A Slack watcher: poll the bot's channels; a thread matching a rule stages a candidate.
watchers.name: mentions
watchers.//trigger: type 'slack' — a thread qualifies when one of 'mentions' is @-mentioned anywhere in it (including a late reply); 'mentions' is required and non-empty (fail-closed). 'channels' are Slack channel IDs the bot has been invited to (ALL are scanned, in parallel, each with its own cursor) OR the string "auto" to auto-discover every channel the bot is a member of. Friendly names (#channel) need the read-only channels:read/groups:read scope; otherwise the id is shown.
watchers.//trigger-excludeChannels: Optional denylist, and what makes "auto" practical: keep discovering every channel the bot joins, but never scan these — use it to mute a busy alert channel that never actually mentions you. Ids, not names. Excluding a channel also drops its tracked threads (reclaiming the tracked-thread budget) but keeps its cursor, so removing it from this list backfills the gap rather than skipping it. Never reconciled against discovery: an id for a channel the bot has left stays excluded, so re-inviting the bot cannot quietly resume it. Unlike the temporary per-channel pause in the UI, this survives a state reset.
watchers.//rules: Your when -> then map. The classifier matches a qualifying thread to ONE named rule (or none); the action comes from this map, not from the model. 'about' is what the rule matches, in plain words. action.type is 'skill' (runs that skill) or 'prompt' (schema-ready; the runner treats it as no skill for now). Empty list = the model picks a skill freely (looser).

rules.name: pr-review
rules.about: asked to review a pull request

rules.name: bug
rules.about: a bug, failure, or regression to investigate

watchers.//poll: How often to poll (seconds; floored at 30). A persistent cursor backfills anything missed while the machine was asleep.
watchers.//action.preferCheckout: NOT YET HONORED per watcher — the tie-break the runner uses comes from the CLAUDE_DASH_PREFER_CHECKOUT env var. Accepted and preserved here for when it is wired through. Meaning: when a repo is checked out under more than one parent folder, prefer the one whose parent folder has this name.
watchers.//action.cwd: Optional fallback target folder. A candidate's cwd is normally derived from a PR link in the message; if none resolves, this folder is used so the candidate is still launchable. Omit to leave such candidates without a cwd.

watchers.//: A GitHub review watcher: ask GitHub which PRs are waiting on YOUR review and stage each as a candidate. No token here — it speaks through the `gh` CLI you are already logged into. Use this instead of trying to read a review queue out of Slack: a channel subscribed to an org receives repo activity with no reviewer information, and the personally-addressed "X requested your review" notification is a DM a bot token cannot read.
watchers.name: reviews
watchers.//trigger: type 'github'. 'search' is a GitHub search query (default: review-requested:@me is:open is:pr) — narrow it per watcher, e.g. add org:myorg. 'login' is optional; blank means ask `gh` who you are. 'first' caps how many PRs one query returns (max 100).

trigger.//jiraProjects: Issue-key prefixes that are REAL project keys. Multiple PRs on one story are grouped into a single candidate so they can be reviewed together, and the grouping signal is a shared key — so a stray standards id must never look like one. Without this list a built-in denylist (SHA, CVE, RFC, …) is used instead; SHA-256 appearing in both a real PR body and a bot's release notes once chained an unrelated version bump into a genuine story.
trigger.//authors: Set excludeAuthors OR includeAuthors, never both. Bots are excluded by default: the [bot] suffix, plus known logins that carry no suffix (GitHub reports Dependabot as plain 'dependabot' on dependency PRs). includeAuthors inverts the filter, which is how you run a SECOND watcher that batches exactly the bot PRs this one drops — with its own prompt and skill, no code change.
trigger.//skipDrafts: Draft PRs are skipped by default.
trigger.//maxGroupSize: Cap PRs per story candidate, so one very widely-cited epic cannot collapse the queue into a single unreviewable item.
trigger.//maxStagePerTick: New candidates staged per poll. A first run against a long-standing queue fills gradually instead of dumping ~30 at once; the rest arrive on later ticks.
trigger.//group: 'story' (default): PRs sharing an issue key become one candidate. 'all': the ENTIRE selection folds into one digest candidate — pair with includeAuthors for a bot-PR watcher that batches every dependency bump into a single card; a changed queue supersedes the previous pending digest.

watchers.//rules: For a github watcher, rules map a DETECTED STACK to a review skill: name the rule after the stack. The stack comes from the repo's build file (go.mod → go, pom.xml/build.gradle → java), so no LLM is involved and this keeps working when the headless classifier does not. A story whose repos all resolve to one skill carries it; a genuinely mixed Go+Java story carries none and the prompt names them per repo.
watchers.//poll: The review queue moves on human timescales and costs one API call, so it polls far less often than a Slack channel. Default 900s.
watchers.//prompt: Optional prompt template. Placeholders: {story} {prs} {repos} {skills} {coherence}. Omit for the built-in light hand-off — which PRs, which story, which repo paths, which skill. Deliberately NOT a pre-solved brief: the review smarts belong in the skill, which runs fresh at launch.
watchers.//action.cwd: Fallback folder when a PR's repo is not checked out locally, so the candidate is still launchable.

watchers.//: A scheduled prompt watcher: NOT RUN YET (schema + validation only — the runner executes 'slack' triggers today; see docs/proposals.md Proposal 6). It is reported in the Watchers tab as not-implemented rather than silently ignored.
watchers.name: morning-pr-sweep
watchers.//trigger: type 'schedule' — one of everyMinutes / at ("HH:MM", means daily) / cron.
watchers.//skill: Optional. The producer session starts as /<skill> with 'prompt' as its arguments; omit or leave empty to run the prompt on its own.
watchers.//prompt: The producing task. The watcher appends a 'report done / what blocked' step and a run token automatically; the session only stages candidates — launching one stays your click.
watchers.prompt: Check my review-requested pull requests. For each new one, stage a candidate with the right review skill and a precise brief. If a tool is unauthenticated or you need a decision you can't safely make, stop and say exactly what is blocking.
watchers.//action.cwd: The folder the producer session opens in, and the fallback for a candidate it stages without a resolvable repo.
